question: Why is Māyā's transformation not a defect in its imperishable nature?
premises: Māyā is the imperishable material cause.
Transformation can occur in only a part of a whole.
The ghee-worm analogy illustrates partial transformation.
inference: Therefore Māyā transforms by one part alone and there is no fault.
uncertainties: pariṇamata taken as finite verb in context
plain_english: By the analogy of the ghee-worm, Māyā transforms by one part alone; thus there is no fault.
